provenance: Written from working knowledge. Gene-disease relationships are well established; CELL-TYPE ATTRIBUTIONS ARE SIMPLIFICATIONS — most of these genes act in several cell types, and the primary-cell column names where the mechanism is usually described. Not clinical guidance.

cells.name: Plasmacytoid dendritic cell
cells.role: The main producer of type I interferon

cells.name: B cell
cells.role: Presents antigen, matures into the antibody-producing plasma cell

cells.name: Plasma cell
cells.role: Secretes autoantibodies; long-lived and largely drug-resistant

cells.name: T cell
cells.role: Provides help to B cells; the Tfh subset drives germinal centres

cells.name: Monocyte / macrophage
cells.role: Clears apoptotic debris — the failure that starts the cycle

cells.name: Neutrophil
cells.role: NETosis releases chromatin, feeding the nucleic-acid sensors

cells.name: Kidney resident cell
cells.role: Where immune-complex deposition becomes organ damage

axes.name: Clearance of dying cells
axes.note: Debris that is not cleared becomes the antigen.

axes.name: Nucleic-acid sensing
axes.note: Self DNA/RNA read as if it were viral.

axes.name: Type I interferon
axes.note: The amplifier; the signature most SLE patients carry.

axes.name: B-cell tolerance
axes.note: Autoreactive B cells that should have been deleted.

axes.name: Complement
axes.note: Paradox: deficiency causes lupus, consumption marks it.

monogenic.note: C1q deficiency is the strongest known single-gene risk for lupus — over 90% of those affected develop it. Also the cleanest statement of the clearance model.
Early classical-pathway deficiency, same mechanism as C1q.
Complement C4 copy number varies between people, so 'the gene' is not even a fixed quantity — dosage is the risk factor.
Commonest classical-pathway deficiency; lower penetrance than C1q.
Cannot degrade extracellular chromatin. Causes early-onset lupus with anti-dsDNA — the antigen is literally the undigested debris.
A cytosolic DNase; its loss leaves self DNA to be sensed as viral. Also causes Aicardi-Goutieres syndrome — the same gene, a different disease, by dose.
The interferonopathy genes. Lupus and Aicardi-Goutieres sit on one continuum of nucleic-acid handling.
GAIN of function — the sensor is constitutively on. The therapeutic logic inverts: you want less signal, not more gene.
STING gain of function (SAVI). Vasculopathy with lupus features.
Loss of B-cell apoptosis; autoreactive clones survive selection.
A20 haploinsufficiency. Also a common-variant SLE locus — the same gene appears as an ultra-rare mendelian cause and as a small-effect population risk.
ALPS; lupus-like autoimmunity from failed lymphocyte apoptosis.

sle.name: Systemic lupus erythematosus
sle.note: SLE sits ON the rare-disease boundary rather than inside or outside it. The EU threshold is 5 in 10 000 (= 50 per 100 000). Reported SLE prevalence spans roughly 20-150 per 100 000 depending on population, ancestry and case definition — so the same disease is legally rare in one country and not in another, and the deciding factor is partly who was counted.
sle.disparity: Prevalence and severity are substantially higher in people of African, Hispanic and Asian ancestry than in European-ancestry populations. Most genetic studies were done in the latter, so the evidence base is thinnest where the burden is heaviest.

therapies.name: Anifrolumab
therapies.note: Blocks the amplifier rather than the trigger — the interferon signature made actionable.

therapies.name: Rituximab
therapies.note: Depletes B cells but spares CD20-negative plasma cells, which is the usual explanation for incomplete responses.

therapies.name: CD19 CAR-T
therapies.note: The result that reframed the field: deep B-cell depletion has produced drug-free remission in refractory SLE. A CELL therapy, not a gene therapy — the unit of intervention is the cell, which is the point of this section.

therapies.name: Anti-CD38 / plasma-cell directed
therapies.note: Aimed at the long-lived plasma cell that B-cell depletion leaves behind.
